source.title: Edge of Stability Selectively Shapes Learning Across the Data Distribution
source.authors: Shauna Kwag; Anakha Ganesh; Tomaso A. Poggio; Pierfrancesco Beneventano

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally tests how full-batch gradient descent behaves at the edge of stability on per-group losses and gradient alignment, a related training-dynamics question, but it does not test the claim versions about reaching near-zero classification error, depth, initialization, learning-rate recovery, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on EoS effects on prototype-group losses, gradients, and test-time robustness/generalization. Only training-loss, alignment, and curvature-influence results bear on the listed versions; classification-error results are not reported. Values available only in figures are recorded as figure only. The paper cites prior EoS results, which are not treated as its own findings.
record.test_reason: The study's own full-batch gradient-descent experiments measure top Hessian sharpness rising to and remaining near the stability threshold while training losses decrease. These directly bear on V5's edge-of-stability clause, using the method and measures of Cohen et al.; testing initial learning-rate recovery is not required to test this separate clause.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that EoS redistributes learning across subsets, with benefits governed jointly by directional alignment and gradient persistence. Robustness and generalization consequences depend on the dominant subset and remain preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch gradient descent with an EoS branching intervention and per-group loss/alignment measurements; it does not apply the original interventions or outcome measures in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The beneficiary changes with prototype geometry/class pair and loss function; coherent versus random-direction displacement changes alignment and the EoS trade-off. The authors also report effects across architecture and optimizer settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Remaining at EoS accelerates loss reduction for some prototype groups and suppresses it for others; alignment and gradient persistence determine the beneficiaries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Edge-of-stability dynamics selectively redistribute training progress across data subsets according to gradient alignment and persistence.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarial robustness and extrapolation benefits change with the group dominating the constrained direction; these preliminary evaluations use single seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization consequences of EoS depend on which data subsets dominate its constrained direction.

record.problems: Experiments are restricted to relatively small models and datasets, primarily full-batch training. Robustness and generalization results are described as preliminary and include single-seed figures. Several primary findings are shown in figures rather than numerical tables.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the paper's reported measures do not test any of V1–V6. EoS-related findings concern per-subset loss, alignment, curvature influence, robustness, and OOD loss, rather than the training-error, local-minima, depth, initialization, learning-rate-recovery, or batch-normalization outcomes those versions name.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random labels, and its dependence on size, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of activation-matched, orthogonal, or Gaussian initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Initial catapult loss rise and recovery above the initial linearized stability limit; divergence at larger learning rates; divergence despite starting below the threshold.
Batch normalization versus matched unnormalized networks, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Extract paired sharpness and training-loss trajectories for the primary full-batch experiment: baseline sharpness approaches and stays near 200 as losses decrease; halving the learning rate raises the threshold to 400 and temporarily exits EoS. The blanket exclusion in rows_left_out incorrectly treats these direct V5 measurements as unrelated.

Extract additional full-batch sharpness trajectories and corresponding loss progress across CNN, normalization-free ResNet-14, and cat-versus-dog settings, keeping architecture and data conditions separate.
missing.locator: Appendix C.1, Figures 11–12; Appendix C.3, Figures 16–17

record.verdict_notes: Selective subgroup progress does not challenge V5's global training-dynamics statement. No numerical loss endpoints are recoverable from the supplied figure text. Figure 17's caption conflicts with Section 5.1 and Appendix C.3 about the beneficiary at α = 10; this does not affect the V5 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels; effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Whether two-layer ReLU teacher-student gradient descent reaches spurious local minima and how extra student neurons affect that outcome.
Whether plain networks degrade with depth and identity shortcuts prevent it; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and training plain networks at greater depth.
Recovery or divergence at learning rates above stability limits and sharpness behavior over longer full-batch training.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gain or increases learning-rate tolerance, and whether Fixup matches normalized residual training.

relationships.condition: Full-batch GD, width-512 two-hidden-layer ReLU MLP, binary CIFAR-10 with prototype groups, MSE, learning rate 0.01.
relationships.reason: Text and Figure 4 show sharpness reaching and remaining near 2/η = 200 while prototype training losses continue decreasing; the half-rate branch exits this regime and subsequently reaches its new threshold. No result rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness reached and remained near 2/η = 200 while prototype losses decreased, and halving the rate temporarily exited this regime before reaching the new threshold.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
